proposal_S_measurement.claim: The S4 truncation is not caused by the batch size. It is caused by fact_ids being bounded neither in element content nor in count, which gives a sampled reply an unbounded sink and gives the decoder a zero-cost way to satisfy the array with strings that name no fact.

Nothing was written into the transaction and no tracked file was edited; the schema variant below was mutated in memory only.

proposal_S_measurement.what_the_samples_establish: The identical request completes in 2,770 tokens at the identical budget with the identical prompt token count, so 32,000 is a property of one sample, not of the request - which makes jobs.py's 'a re-ask under the same budget cannot help' false for this job. Every completed sample as shipped is rejected anyway: every fact_ids string it returns is a bare <kind>: prefix that names no fact, 27 of 27 in one sample and 67 of 107 in the other, and binding_errors raises 8 unknown fact IDs against it. Requiring one character after the colon removes both: 133 real IDs, zero bare prefixes, binding down from 8 errors to 1.
